title: Guardrails for a board that can now rewrite its own rules

notes: [2026-09-15T11:15:46.876Z] Decision: split the write surface in two. Item-level writes (create, move, edit, note, triage, resume, dispatch, stop) stay available wherever the board is reachable — that is the collaborative surface and the reason --host exists. Administrative writes that change the rules of the board itself (stages, gates, config) are refused unless the request arrived on loopback, regardless of --host. Rationale: a colleague on the LAN moving a card is the feature; a stranger on hotel wifi deleting your stages, disabling a gate, or enabling the runner is not. The guard is cheap, needs no auth system, and keeps the property that gw serve never becomes a remote administration console.

title: move: every refusal must name a command that actually works
scope: stageOrderMessage promises an actionable next step and breaks that promise in two cases, on every board, not only trunk-shaped ones. (1) Last pipeline stage: nextStage() returns null, so the 'outside the pipeline' branch fires even though fromIndex >= 0, and the backward branch that would have given the right answer is never reached. (2) Any side stage: the shipped board's own 'paused' and 'dropped' are outside the pipeline, so re-entering the pipeline prints 'move it onto the pipeline first: run gw move <id> backlog' — and that command is refused by the same rule, verbatim, forever. Both are dead ends: the one thing this function exists to prevent. Done when every branch names a command move would accept, the last stage and the side stages are covered by tests on both a trunk and the shipped pipeline, and the agent contract distinguishes --force for pipeline ORDER (lawful, and named by the refusal itself) from --force past a GATE (never).

title: Windows: containment and the executable bit
scope: CI on windows-latest failed three of the new tests. One real defect: --pretool judged 'outside the repository' with relative().startsWith('..'), and between two drives Windows cannot express that answer as '..' — it returns the target absolute — so /etc/hosts read as inside the repo and was gated. Fixed by moving the containment predicate root.js already had into lib/util/paths.js as isWithin() and using it at both call sites, per specs §10.2 / P6-02: every comparison against an OS-produced path normalises first. Two platform-honesty fixes: hook status reported 'not executable' on Windows, which has no such bit for git to consult (Git for Windows runs the hook through its bundled sh regardless); and the two tests that need a POSIX shell and a ':' PATH separator now skip there, with the unit coverage reaching the same decisions without a shell. Done when all three OSes are green in CI.
